answer: One defense is a bonded, hardware-attested agent registry: each agent proves it runs in a unique secure enclave, posts a slashable stake, and receives a non-transferable credential. The registry caps credentials per operator and enforces a cool-down, so a Sybil farm cannot mint identities in parallel; duplicate attestations mirror one another and are rejected. Revoked credentials remain as a public relic, and a small proof-of-useful-work fee, recorded in shale-like strata, makes bulk registration costly.
